title: Count Enabled Permissions
real_world_story: A security system stores user permissions as a binary permission mask. Every set bit represents one enabled permission, and the system needs to determine how many permissions are currently active.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Binary permission mask stored as an integer
real_world_connection.target_represents: Number of permissions enabled for the user
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Counting the set bits in the permission mask

problem_statement: Given a non-negative integer representing a user's permission mask, count the number of set bits, or 1s, in its binary representation.
task: Determine the number of enabled permissions represented by the set bits.
input_format: The input contains a single non-negative integer N representing the permission mask.
output_format: Print the number of set bits in the binary representation of N.

examples.explanation: 29 is 11101 in binary, which contains four set bits.
16 is 10000 in binary, so exactly one permission bit is enabled.

expected_algorithm.name: Count Set Bits
expected_algorithm.reason: Counting set bits determines how many individual permissions are enabled in a permission mask.

hint: Inspect the binary representation of the permission mask.
Count every bit whose value is 1.
The operation N & (N - 1) can remove the lowest set bit efficiently.
real_world_takeaway: Counting set bits is useful when permission systems store many enabled or disabled access features inside a compact binary mask.
